hook: A deadpan, deeply strange file built around a table: what to do when a traveler shows you their ID, offers money, or smiles. The image caption and the containment procedures already signal how odd this is going to get. One row of the table briefly describes a traveler peeling the skin off their own face.
whyItMatters: 2771 flips the usual setup by making the Foundation the confused party: armed guards are being taken for a job nobody explains, and the only countermeasure is to get good at the job. Nearly the whole article is the procedure document, pieced together through failures and written with complete seriousness. The response-table format carries the humor and the unease at the same time.
thingsToNotice: SCP-2771-1 wear badly cut cloth copies of black tactical gear and green uniforms, talk only by pointing two fingers or showing annoyance, and redo their captives' clothes with chalk, paint and sackcloth before sending them to a desert tollbooth beside a transit system shaped like a rippling human tongue. Fighting them only brings more of them, so Area-2771 keeps at least fifteen trained, armed staff in matching outfits on hand, and other sites are told to keep pointing at its location on a map until the visitors leave. Procedure 366-Tutella is pure trial and error with no logic offered: bite off part of a laminated ID and hand back the rest wrapped in foil, slide cash under your forearm and later split it with your abductors, and answer a traveler peeling away their face with nothing more than visible impatience. The only time the sidearm comes out is when a traveler smiles, after which the road twists into a helix and swallows whoever was hurt or killed. A footnote adds that every bill recovered so far is ordinary modern currency.
